Title: These 7 principles make your emails more fun to read. (while adding cash to your bottom line)
Body1_P1: You can steal these 7 principles I use to inject more fun into your emails and get your readers coming back for more.
Body2_P1: Sassy sales scripts that sell without sounding slimy. Your brain remembers how copy SOUNDS before what it says.
Body2_P2: Rewrite for beat not grammar. Alliteration and sticky lines make info land when facts alone wouldn't.
Body3_P1: Selling without a plan is like baking without a recipe — messy and disappointing.
Body3_P2: Don't explain harder. Translate. Hand them a mental picture and let their brain do the work.
Body4_P1: Tease the payoff early. Deliver it later. I'll tell you the weirdest trick I learned… but first a quick story.
Body4_P2: Your reader's brain hates unfinished business. That tension is what pulls them to the next paragraph.
Body5_P1: Not a bad sales call. 37 cold calls in a row — rejected by everyone except the guy eating a tuna sandwich.
Body5_P2: Vague sounds like AI. Specific sounds like a human was in the room. The detail just has to be picture-able.
Body6_P1: I'd rather wrestle a raccoon for pizza than read another three-point AI email. Humor disarms before the ask.
Body6_P2: Boring is the only unforgivable sin in copy. One tiny chuckle buys you three more paragraphs of attention.
Body7_P1: Write like you're talking to one person. Short sentences. Questions. You and I — not dear valued customer.
Body7_P2: Say it out loud. If it sounds like a press release? Rewrite it. Your inbox isn't a boardroom.
CTA_Question: Call out their situation. Ask rhetorical questions. End lists with a punchline — more sales, less stress, smug superiority over your competition.
CTA_Steps: Talk WITH them not AT them. That's the difference between content they finish and content they secretly skip.
